methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Aestus Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $10M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable, all operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector. The private peer set includes later-stage companies such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics, providing relevant benchmarks for capital-intensive frontier technology.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, anchoring to the $10M total raised as a proxy for current valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding $20M. The peer-median method examines the four sampled comparables—which range from Seed to Series B stage—and identifies a median valuation of $1.7B across the $1.1B to $2.0B range. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in stage and capital efficiency across the peer set.

The triangulated analysis produces a low estimate of $17M and a high estimate of $2.0B, with a median of $860M. This wide band reflects material uncertainty inherent in valuing an early-stage frontier technology company against both later-stage peers and limited precedent for capital requirements and commercialization timelines in robotics manufacturing. The stage-progression method suggests a near-term floor, while peer multiples anchor upside under successful execution. Key sensitivities include the pace of Series B fundraising, path to revenue, and consolidation dynamics among later-stage peers.
